players.product: AI / HPC data-center campuses on owned powered land (Hannibal campus with pending Long Ridge, Matagorda County TX; developed with Starwood) plus Exaion sovereign private cloud for AI inference in Europe

quarterly_data.quarter: MARA Holdings h.c. wainwright global investment conference 2026 (09-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Fred Thiel: MARA took majority control of Exaion, a former subsidiary of EDF, in a deal that closed in March of this year; Exaion has already started taking contracts hosting U.S. inference and training loads in Europe because of delays in getting capacity online in the U.S., and MARA will bring Exaion's expertise in running mission-critical data centers to build onshore in the U.S. at its smaller sites, which often do not make sense for a hyperscaler or another neocloud. Thiel said MARA went after Exaion to run fully air-gapped, fully sovereign inference at scale for enterprises: about 60% of AI workloads today are fairly mundane, running dedicated hardware in Amazon Web Services is a 10X higher cost than private cloud, and he expects a lot more inference to move behind the firewall or to near-prem / on-prem inference providers running sovereign models - 'by far the biggest thing moving forward in this industry.'
quarterly_data.figure: Exaion deal closed in March; about 60% of AI workloads mundane; 10X cost of dedicated public-cloud hardware vs private cloud (CEO view)

quarterly_data.quarter: MARA Holdings h.c. wainwright global investment conference 2026 (09-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Fred Thiel: MARA does not announce LOIs or exclusivities around leases but feels very confident about signing the two leases by year-end, with activity expected at both small and large sites; tenant size requirements range from 400-500 megawatts in some cases to 50-150 megawatts in others. Large sites such as Matagorda can scale significantly north of 500 megawatts with multiple tenants, letting MARA optimize pricing by tenant credit, lease duration and use case - for example a hyperscaler on a triple net lease at a yield on cost of 10%, a neocloud at 15% yield on cost, and enterprise clients at an even higher level.
quarterly_data.figure: two leases by year-end; tenant requirements 400-500 MW or 50-150 MW; yield on cost ~10% (hyperscaler triple net) vs 15% (neocloud)

quarterly_data.quarter: MARA Holdings h.c. wainwright global investment conference 2026 (09-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Fred Thiel: MARA partnered with Starwood - which has built over 7 gigawatts of data center capacity for hyperscalers and has a captive EPCM - to increase delivery certainty and reduce risk, as MARA is not an expert in building data centers for hyperscaler demands. In these joint ventures MARA contributes its site as equity, so in an 80/20 model the additional capital it must put in over and above the value of its site is fairly de minimis, giving significantly greater cash-on-cash returns and letting it develop more sites in parallel without all of the credit being provided by MARA.
quarterly_data.figure: Starwood over 7 gigawatts built; site contributed as equity in an 80/20 model

quarterly_data.quarter: MARA Holdings h.c. wainwright global investment conference 2026 (09-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Fred Thiel: Bitcoin mining infrastructure and compute typically cost somewhere around $1 million, $1.5 million a megawatt, very different from AI HPC, where revenue and asset value per megawatt provide a considerable step-up. MARA's model converts Bitcoin mining sites to AI: mining is load it can turn on immediately while waiting for energization, and as an AI tenant moves into the data center MARA deprecates mining there and moves it to another acquired site. Because the cost of Bitcoin mining ASICs has never been as low on a per terahash basis, MARA's exahash capacity does not have to shrink as the megawatt capacity allocated to Bitcoin shrinks.
quarterly_data.figure: Bitcoin mining build cost around $1 million, $1.5 million a megawatt
